text:
anna: heads-up, hitting a weird HF->Redwood conversion failure during bring-up for `opus-small`. tokenizer.json exists but `tokenizer_config.json` is missing. fast loader accepts it, slow (py-tokenizer) throws — evals show token id drift :confused:

josh: can you paste the small error? also which loader path is used (fast/slow)? :eyes:

anna: stack trace (trimmed):
```
File "/opt/redwood/runtime/token_load.py", line 142, in load_tokenizer
  cfg = read_json(path / 'tokenizer_config.json')
FileNotFoundError: tokenizer_config.json

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
ValueError: special tokens mismatch: expected keys ['bos_token','eos_token'] found ['start_token']
```

sara: hm this rings a bell — some HF exports write everything into `tokenizer.json` (fast) but the slow loader expects the separate `tokenizer_config.json` with `special_tokens_map`. If both exist we prefer slow. If only one present we try to translate, but our translator is brittle.

mike: repro steps i used: `git checkout bringup/opus-small` then `python -m redwood.tools.convert_hf --src ./hf_model --out ./package`. The converter emitted `tokenizer.json` and `vocab.json` but NOT `tokenizer_config.json`. 

anna: quick diff of token fields: `tokenizer.json` has `special_tokens: {"start_token":"<s>"}` while our runtime expects `special_tokens_map: {"bos_token":"<s>"}`. So the mapping fails at load-time and downstream evals show off-by-one ids in prompts.

josh: can we synth a drop-in `tokenizer_config.json` in the converter as a fallback? simple mapping rules: start_token->bos_token, end_token->eos_token, unk->unk_token.

sara: yes we can. propose a tiny converter patch: when converter sees `tokenizer.json` and no `tokenizer_config.json`, emit `{
  "special_tokens_map": {"bos_token": original.get('special_tokens',{}).get('start_token')},
  "added_tokens": []
}`. also add a `--strict-token-config` flag to fail CI if ambiguous.

ci-bot: note: unit tests failed in PR #4123 showing token id diffs on quantized evals (regression +1.2% perplexity). See: https://ci.redwood.ai/PR/4123/logs

mike: i'll open a tiny PR to synth `tokenizer_config.json` + a test that runs `redwood.tools.convert_hf --smoke` and checks both files exist when `--compat` flag used. assigning to @sara to review if that mapping is safe for chat templates.

anna: quick patch i used locally to rescue a failing VM:
```python
# quick synth from tokenizer.json
import json, pathlib
root = pathlib.Path('./package')
j = json.loads((root/'tokenizer.json').read_text())
map = {
  'bos_token': j.get('special_tokens',{}).get('start_token'),
  'eos_token': j.get('special_tokens',{}).get('end_token')
}
cfg = {'special_tokens_map': {k:v for k,v in map.items() if v}}
(root/'tokenizer_config.json').write_text(json.dumps(cfg))
```

josh: nice. for long-term we should: 1) update converter, 2) add loader warning when only one file present, 3) add an eval that compares tokenization between fast/slow on a small prompt set.

sara: agreed. i'll add a loader warning and a regression test in the tokenizer test-suite. mike, assign the PR to me and I'll do review.

mike: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4782 "converter: synth tokenizer_config.json when absent" — includes smoke test.

anna: thanks all — marking follow-ups: `#1` converter change (mike), `#2` loader warning + strict flag (sara), `#3` fast/slow tokenization parity eval (josh). Re-ran eval after local synth — perplexity diff went back within tolerance. :white_check_mark:
